records.title: T cell redirection in high-risk smouldering multiple myeloma: can deep responses prevent progression to multiple myeloma?
records.description: The randomized phase II ImmunoPRISM trial has shown encouraging efficacy of the B cell maturation antigen-targeted bispecific T cell engager teclistamab in high-risk smouldering multiple myeloma, although several aspects constrain interpretation of the results. Herein, I discuss aspects that should be addressed in future research, such as patient selection, treatment duration, clinically relevant end points and adequate treatment in the control arm, to establish whether deep responses translate into durable prevention of progression with an acceptable benefit–risk profile.

Divarasib outperforms first-generation KRAS-G12C inhibitors in NSCLC

Sacituzumab tirumotecan–pembrolizumab has efficacy in PD-L1-negative NSCLC
Author Correction: Combining locoregional treatments and immunotherapies in patients with unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma
Emerging strategies for paediatric cancer predisposition: detection, surveillance and prevention
records.description: Many childhood cancers occur in children with an underlying predisposition to developing cancer. Thus, identifying individuals with a cancer predisposition syndrome (CPS), ideally before the development of cancer, can enable regular clinical surveillance and potentially the introduction of preventive measures. In this Perspective, the authors describe cancer detection, surveillance and prevention strategies for the management of children with a CPS, as well as the potential of artificial intelligence-based methods to optimize the management of these individuals.

records.title: Phase III data support a novel trifluridine–tipiracil dosing schedule
Reply to: ‘Interpreting surgical consolidation in oligometastatic gastro-oesophageal cancer’
Interpreting surgical consolidation in oligometastatic gastro-oesophageal cancer
Problematic control arms in National Cancer Institute myeloma trials
records.description: Three of five National Cancer Institute-sponsored randomized trials that are currently enrolling patients with multiple myeloma have control arms that no longer reflect the standard of care, despite two of these trials being activated in 2026. Comparators in federally sponsored trials need reassessment and, if necessary, updating to reflect changes in clinical practice before and during enrolment.

records.title: Combining locoregional treatments and immunotherapies in patients with unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma
records.description: Patients with intermediate-stage hepatocellular carcinoma typically receive locoregional therapies (LRTs). Nonetheless, most patients receiving LRTs will have disease progression, indicating a need for earlier use of systemic therapies, which were previously reserved for patients with advanced-stage disease. In this Review, the authors describe data from various studies combining LRTs (including transarterial chemoembolization, transarterial radioembolization and external beam radiotherapy) in patients with intermediate-stage hepatocellular carcinoma, as well as discussing the underlying biological rationale for these combinations and the most promising future research directions.

records.title: No cancer research without older adults, from prevention to end of life: a manifesto
records.description: Older adults (aged ≥65 years) comprise the majority of people diagnosed with cancer, yet they remain proportionally underrepresented in cancer research at every stage of the pathway. We call on funders, regulators, researchers and journals to make systematic inclusion of older adults the norm, across studies spanning from cancer prevention to end-of-life care.

records.title: An imprecise label in the era of precision medicine: labelling and access for daraxonrasib, the first pan-RAS inhibitor approval
records.description: The FDA recently approved daraxonrasib for patients with metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma who received at least one prior systemic therapy or who are not candidates for multiagent systemic therapy. Critics call the second clause non-evidence based. However, this imprecision enables access: trials generally enrol only patients with good performance status, which does not reflect the realities for most patients with metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma who never reach second-line therapy because their clinical condition deteriorates first. Real-world evidence should resolve any remaining uncertainty.

records.title: A modular framework for antibody–drug conjugate biomarkers
records.description: Antibody–drug conjugates (ADCs) have transformed the management of various advanced-stage solid cancers. Nonetheless, and despite considerable development efforts, many of these agents lack reliable biomarkers of clinical benefit and/or are reliant on traditional methods of biomarker assessment, with biomarkers of resistance and/or toxicity largely overlooked. In this Review, the authors outline a modular ADC biomarker development strategy that considers the various components of these agents and discuss how biomarkers developed using this strategy might better inform patient selection, therapeutic sequencing, the development of rational combinations, dose optimization and regulatory strategy.

records.title: Adjuvant radiotherapy improves outcomes in patients with completely resected atypical meningioma
Right-sizing treatment for HER2-positive breast cancer: evolving algorithms across the disease continuum
records.description: The iterative development of several highly effective treatments for HER2-positive breast cancer has transformed patient outcomes, but the now-crowded therapeutic landscape raises questions regarding the optimal approach for each patient. In this Review, the authors outline considerations for right-sizing therapy across the disease continuum, and discuss biomarkers that might facilitate this more individualized approach to treatment.

records.title: Exercise therapy in cancer prevention and treatment
records.description: Exercise is widely endorsed as a supportive-care adjunct to mitigate adverse effects of cancer treatment, with data also suggesting potential therapeutic and preventive roles. In this Review, the authors discuss the current evidence from epidemiological studies and clinical trials for exercise as a factor modulating primary cancer risk and disease outcomes after diagnosis, and describe a translational framework for continued development of exercise therapy and a path towards precision exercise oncology.

records.title: Exploring the immunological effects of antibody–drug conjugates
records.description: Antibody–drug conjugates (ADCs) have reshaped the therapeutic landscape of many advanced-stage cancers. This clinical activity probably reflects mechanisms beyond targeted cytotoxicity, with emerging evidence suggesting an immune-mediated component. At the same time, regimens combining ADCs with immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) are emerging as a highly effective treatment strategy in various malignancies. In this Review, the authors discuss the immunological mechanisms of action of ADCs, their clinical activity in combination with ICIs, as well as the potential of future agents and regimens to further improve outcomes.

records.title: Benefit with post-consolidation blinatumomab in newly diagnosed high-risk B-ALL
Optimizing the delivery of radiotherapy with artificial intelligence
records.description: Radiation oncology involves complex, data-intensive clinical workflows, which makes this medical specialty an ideal setting for leveraging the unique capabilities of artificial intelligence (AI). The authors of this Review present examples of successful AI applications in radiation oncology, present the current challenges for successful clinical implementation of these applications and discuss broader implications, such as the need to ensure safe and optimal use of AI in order to improve patient outcomes.

records.title: Tambotatug pelitecan — a potential new second-line treatment option for SCLC
Understanding and targeting the tumour matrisome
records.description: The extracellular matrix (ECM) has a role in all aspects of cancer progression and thus provides a rich source of potential tumour biomarkers and therapeutic targets. Nonetheless, early efforts at clinical translation have failed to provide ECM-specific clinical tools or therapies. In this Review, the authors describe novel technologies and how these are being leveraged to better inform our understanding of the role of the ECM in cancer development and progression as well as how this new knowledge and capabilities might lead to novel biomarkers and/or ECM-targeting therapies.

records.title: Publisher Correction: Antibody–drug conjugates in gynaecological cancers: opportunities and challenges
Armouring GPC3 CAR T cells for hepatocellular carcinoma: how much is enough and what comes next?
records.description: A new chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cell product consists of autologous T cells expressing an affinity-tuned glypican 3-targeted CAR and armoured to secrete a dominant-negative TGFβ receptor II. This cell product was tested in 36 patients with hepatocellular carcinoma and, although the initial efficacy results were promising, antigen loss and limited progression-free survival remain concerns. Here we discuss what else is needed to bring CAR T cells for solid tumours into the clinic.

records.title: Preliminary efficacy with daraxonrasib demonstrated in RAS-mutant NSCLC
Publisher Correction: Beyond cold to hot: oncolytic virotherapy as the next cornerstone of immuno-oncology
Liver resection improves survival in patients with locally advanced HCC
Beyond cold to hot: oncolytic virotherapy as the next cornerstone of immuno-oncology
records.description: The development of diverse immunotherapeutic modalities has revolutionized the treatment of cancer but the effectiveness of these therapies remains restricted by fundamental mechanistic limitations relating to the generation of tumour-specific T cells, and their activation and/or access into the tumour microenvironment. In this Perspective, the authors position oncolytic viruses as a foundational immuno-oncology platform for systemic immune reprogramming to simultaneously overcome these availability, activation and admission barriers, and delineate four pillars for the development of a new generation of oncolytic virotherapies.

records.title: Belzutifan plus lenvatinib delays disease progression in advanced-stage RCC
Global cancer statistics 2024: translating epidemiological trends into priorities for healthcare systems
records.description: The global cancer burden is projected to rise substantially in the coming decades, driven largely by population growth and ageing. Yet cancer patterns and outcomes vary widely across regions, reflecting differences in exposures, healthcare capacity and access to care. Translating these evolving epidemiological patterns into effective and equitable cancer-control strategies is increasingly urgent.

records.title: Exploring the landscape of targetable alterations in patients with glioblastoma
records.description: Despite considerable progress in other cancer types, progress with the development of targeted therapies for patients with glioblastoma has remained limited, despite considerable research effort. In this Review, the authors summarize the various attempts to develop effective targeted therapies for patients with glioblastoma, including some of the challenges that have likely impaired progress thus far. The authors also highlight novel therapies, clinical trial designs and research directions that have been informed by the shortcomings of previous research efforts, all of which might eventually lead to improved outcomes for patients.

records.title: Precision oncology needs precision trial design: lessons from FGFR2 -rearranged cholangiocarcinoma
records.description: The phase III FIGHT-302 trial demonstrated that the FGFR inhibitor pemigatinib improves progression-free survival and response rates versus first-line chemotherapy in patients with advanced-stage FGFR2 -rearranged cholangiocarcinoma. However, the trial accrued slowly and closed early after chemoimmunotherapy became the new standard of care. FIGHT-302, alongside two similarly terminated trials, highlights the need for innovative trial designs and flexible regulatory frameworks to evaluate therapies in rare, biomarker-defined populations.

records.title: How positive was PROTEUS? Reconsidering success when most patients never reach no evidence of disease
records.description: PROTEUS met its amended co-primary end points but should not be interpreted as practice changing. The trial compared two experimental strategies rather than the current standard of care, relied on an unvalidated approach (prostate-specific membrane antigen-PET) for assessments of metastasis-free survival, demonstrated minimal absolute benefit with increased toxicity and lacks both mature overall survival data and sufficient data on patient-reported outcomes to support adoption.

records.title: The proteome comes of age, but precision oncology needs functional maps
records.description: Yue and colleagues present a landmark anatomical atlas of human protein abundance across non-malignant tissues and cancers. We argue that precision oncology needs functional proteomic maps that add signalling activity, post-translational modifications, pathology-guided compartment resolution, metastatic and longitudinal sampling, clinical annotation and population diversity to make proteomics therapeutically actionable.

records.title: HCT–ASCT confirmed as standard-of-care consolidation therapy for PCNSL
AI-based augmentation of oncology clinical trials
records.description: Oncology clinical trials are characterized by high failure rates — reflecting both the biological complexity of cancer and operational inefficiencies — and the generalizability of their results is often limited. In this Review, the authors discuss opportunities to address these limitations via application of artificial intelligence tools across the lifecycle of clinical trials as well as key challenges that must be overcome for routine clinical deployment of these tools.

records.title: Benefit from perioperative enfortumab vedotin–pembrolizumab in cisplatin-eligible MIBC
More options, more questions in the management of early relapsed and/or refractory multiple myeloma
records.description: In MonumenTAL-3, the G-protein-coupled receptor class C group 5 memberD-directed bispecific T cell engager talquetamab combined with either daratumumab or daratumumab–pomalidomide conferred significantly longer progression-free survival than daratumumab–pomalidomide–dexamethasone in patients with relapsed and/or refractory multiple myeloma (≥1 prior line of therapy). These results herald a new therapeutic option for such patients but also raise questions regarding how talquetamab-based regimens should be integrated with B cell maturation antigen-directed T cell-redirecting therapies.

records.title: Clinical toxicity of ADCs and ICI–ADC combinations: mechanisms, patterns and management
records.description: With the expanded use of antibody–drug conjugates (ADCs) and immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) in combination, clinicians increasingly face overlapping toxicity profiles with uncertain attribution. The authors of this Review propose a framework that links three interacting layers: immune activation, payload cytotoxicity and payload-independent effects, and provide practical algorithms for evaluation, initial management and treatment resumption in patients receiving ADC monotherapy or ICI–ADC combinations.

records.title: De-escalation trials in multiple myeloma: past, present and future
records.description: Current treatment approaches for patients with multiple myeloma are characterized by a ‘more is better’ philosophy aiming for deep and long-term clinical responses. The authors of this Review challenge this paradigm, presenting several de-escalation strategies that do not compromise long-term efficacy and proposing a framework for the design of trials testing further de-escalation approaches.

records.title: Electronic cigarettes, smoking and lung cancer risk: some evidence about the continuum of harm
records.description: Since the introduction of vaping with electronic cigarettes in the late 2000s, controversy has continued to exist regarding the risks and benefits. Many studies indicate that electronic cigarettes are an effective smoking-cessation tool. Now, a large database analysis by Kim et al. provides a glimpse of the risks of lung cancer for smokers who quit with versus without vaping.

records.title: Towards liquid biopsy-based analysis of antitumour immunity
records.description: Advances in multimodal analyses of diverse cell types and cellular products present in the blood have presented opportunities to non-invasively and repeatedly assess systemic immune dynamics, predict and monitor responses to immunotherapies, and detect emerging resistance in patients with cancer. In this Review, the authors discuss various insights on systemic antitumour immune responses that can be gleaned through such liquid biopsy-based analysis of circulating tumour-derived biomarkers and/or immune cells and their implications for immunotherapy.

records.title: Does OptiTROP-Lung05 open a new frontier for first-line ADC–ICI combinations in NSCLC?
records.description: Interim data from the phase III OptiTROP-Lung05 trial demonstrate that adding the TROP2-targeted antibody–drug conjugate sacituzumab tirumotecan to pembrolizumab improves progression-free survival in patients with PD-L1-positive advanced-stage non-small-cell lung cancer. Herein, I present several questions that need to be addressed before this combination can be considered a new standard of care, such as effect on overall survival, long-term safety, global generalizability and biomarker refinement.

records.title: Second-line 177 Lu-edotreotide shows promise in GEP NETs
Crossover does not confound, it informs: 177 lutetium-PSMA-617 as an example
records.description: Crossover in trials should not be viewed as confounding, but as informative. Crossover reveals whether deferring therapy produces outcomes comparable to those from earlier use. Statistical crossover-adjustment methods carry unaccounted biases and limited clinical utility. Crossover should instead guide treatment-sequencing decisions, weighing toxicity and cost against any overall survival benefit from earlier intervention.

records.title: The future of ciltacabtagene autoleucel in multiple myeloma has just begun
Ciltacabtagene autoleucel heralds the arrival of fixed-duration therapies in myeloma
CRISPR in clinical oncology: translational advances from molecular diagnostics to therapeutics
records.description: CRISPR–Cas technologies provide a modular, programmable platform for sequence-specific targeting of DNA or RNA and have advanced from experimental molecular biology tools to clinical translation. This Review describes current and emerging applications of CRISPR–Cas platforms in oncology, including their use in discovery research, diagnostics and therapeutics.

records.title: Improving neoadjuvant and perioperative therapy in non-small-cell lung cancer
records.description: Perioperative chemoimmunotherapy, comprising platinum-doublet chemotherapy plus an anti-PD-(L)1 antibody, has become the standard-of-care approach for patients with resectable non-small-cell lung cancer without an actionable driver alteration. However, the development of this approach has thus far been largely empirical, with limited capacity for adaptation of treatment strategies to better meet the needs of individual patients. In this Review, the authors discuss the potential for improvements in the current approach to perioperative therapy, including de-escalation for those with a pathological complete response, the capacity of various baseline and/or dynamic biomarkers to optimize outcomes, and the potential for escalation in patients with early evidence of a lack of responsiveness in the perioperative setting.

records.title: Patient value over patent value: the mandate for open-source oncology
records.description: Modern oncology has built highly efficient pathways for patent-protected innovation, but no equivalent machinery for evaluating and developing promising off-patent therapeutics. Herein, we frame ‘open-source oncology’ as a parallel public-interest infrastructure to test, authorize and implement credible generic agents. Designed to translate ownerless evidence into standard-of-care treatments, this framework applies the same scientific seriousness devoted to proprietary drugs, decoupling clinical value from commercial ownership.

records.title: Cancer burden and control in China: landscape, trends and challenges
records.description: Over the past decades, cancer epidemiology trends have substantially shifted in China, with a rapid increase in incidence of cancers that are most common in high-income countries and a substantial decline in incidence of cancers historically prevalent in China. The authors of this Review provide an overview of cancer epidemiology in China, a major contributor to global cancer burden, and discuss national cancer control policies and targets.

records.title: New standards and new constraints redefine treatment sequencing in platinum-resistant ovarian cancer
records.description: The therapeutic landscape of platinum-resistant ovarian cancer is rapidly evolving, with recent phase III trials demonstrating, for the first time, meaningful overall survival improvements beyond bevacizumab-based therapy. Herein we discuss how trials such as MIRASOL and, more recently, ENGOT-ov65/KEYNOTE-B96 and GOG30173/ENGOT-ov72/ROSELLA have established new standards of care through distinct biologically driven therapies and outline the new challenges that these approaches expose.

records.title: Antibody–drug conjugates in gynaecological cancers: opportunities and challenges
records.description: Three antibody–drug conjugates (ADCs) are currently approved for previously treated gynaecological cancers: mirvetuximab soravtansine for folate receptor-α-positive ovarian cancer, trastuzumab deruxtecan for solid tumours expressing HER2 and tisotumab vedotin for cervical cancer (independent of tissue factor expression). The authors of this Review discuss current priorities in the clinical development of ADCs for gynaecological cancers, such as identifying novel targets, understanding mechanisms of resistance and sequencing strategies, and managing toxicities, highlighting key advances and future opportunities.
